newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil house may hold 2nd vote on reform next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil house may hold 2nd vote on reform next week.

text.p: Brazil's Chamber of Deputies may hold a second and final vote on the government's civil service reform bill next week, an official said.

The Congress official said next Thursday was the earliest possible date for a second round vote on the full floor after the lower house completed its first round ballot by voting on proposed amendments Wednesday night.

But he added it was more likely the vote would be left till later, meaning August was a more likely date because Congress leaders have said they would like to give deputies a week off at the end of July.

The government won a crucial victory Wednesday evening when it managed to scupper an opposition attempt to water down the civil service reforms, regarded as a key tool in helping the public sector rein in spending.

It is likely to face another battle in the second round vote as the opposition has pledged to try and strike down an article in the bill that would allow local authorities to fire workers if their payroll costs exceed 60 percent of net annual receipts.
